We get asked all the time...
“What’s it like working with your partner?” 

The truth?
It’s one of the hardest and most rewarding things we’ve ever done. 

When you own a business together, there’s no real separation between work and home. Work follows you to dinner, into the car, on date nights, and somehow always becomes the last conversation before falling asleep. 😂
There are disagreements, stressful days, long nights, unexpected setbacks, and more problem-solving than we ever imagined.

But it’s also meant celebrating every milestone together because no one truly understands what it took to get here like the person who built it with you. Over the past year, we’ve built more than just a gym. We’ve built resilience, learned to communicate better, trust each other more, and face challenges as a team.

As we get closer to celebrating one year since opening our gym, I feel incredibly grateful. Not just for what we’ve built, but for the people we’ve become throughout the journey. This gym isn’t just four walls and equipment. It’s years of sacrifice, faith, late nights, hard conversations, and believing in each other even when the outcome was uncertain.

Working with your partner isn’t about always agreeing.
It’s about choosing the same dream, even on the hard days. And after everything we’ve been through, I wouldn’t want to build this life, or this dream, with anyone else. ❤️

caption:
“Waiting for the perfect moment never happens. Start messy, start scared, but just start. Execution beats perfection.”

Raw Fitness wasn’t built overnight. It wasn’t easy, it wasn’t perfect, and there were so many moments where we wanted to give up.

We started small, training people in parks, in their offices, and in their homes. No fancy equipment, no big space, just passion and a vision to help people change their lives. But with every step forward came new challenges. There were sleepless nights, doubts creeping in, moments when backing down would’ve been the easier choice.

But we kept showing up. We kept fighting. We kept believing.

From those humble beginnings came our very first studio. And inside those walls, something powerful happened, we built a family. A community of people who trusted us, who pushed through their own struggles, who transformed their bodies and their lives. Watching them grow reminded us why we started and fueled us to keep going.

Deep down, we knew there was more. That’s why we decided to take the biggest leap yet: creating Raw Fitness Health Club.

It hasn’t been easy. Building this space took everything we had, sacrifice, relentless work, and a belief that fitness can change lives, because it changed ours. We’ve turned to fitness during the lowest points in our own journeys, and now we’ve created a space where others can do the same.

A year from now, you’ll look back. You’ll either see how far you’ve come, or wish you had started today.

The time will pass anyway. The question is, what will you do with it?

Your body is always responding to how you treat it. 🔑

Eating less isn’t always the answer… especially when you’ve been under eating for a long time. Your body can start adapting, conserving energy, increasing cravings, lowering energy output, and holding onto fuel because it doesn’t trust food is consistently coming in.

Fat loss shouldn’t feel like punishment.
The goal is to fuel your body properly while creating a realistic calorie deficit you can actually maintain long term.

Sometimes the answer isn’t eating less.
Sometimes it’s finally supporting your body properly.

caption:
A month ago… 🇯🇵 

Japan felt like a reminder of a different way of living.
There was beauty in the simplicity of things, respect woven into everyday moments, and a quiet sense of harmony that seemed to exist everywhere. Even in the busiest places, there was a feeling of presence and intention.

Kyoto, especially, invited me to slow down…to notice more, rush less, and appreciate the things we often take for granted.

But what made this trip truly special was experiencing it with my family. There was something deeply healing about seeing my parents take it all in…the temples, the gardens, the streets, the culture. As we get older, time together feels less guaranteed and more precious. Sharing these moments reminded me that sometimes the greatest gift of travel isn’t the place itself, but who you experience it with.

Some trips leave you with memories. The best ones leave you with perspective.
Grateful for both. ✨🙏🏼

caption:
You’re in the gym… but nothing’s really changing. 

It’s usually not one big mistake just a few things that aren’t aligned:

1. Your nutrition doesn’t match your goal ➡️Trying to build muscle but under-eating. Trying to lose fat but over-snacking. You can’t out-train a misaligned diet.

2. Your recovery isn’t supporting your training➡️ You’re training hard… but sleeping 5–6 hours, skipping rest days, and running on empty. Recovery isn’t lazy it’s where the results actually happen.

3. You’re not progressively overloading➡️ Same weights, same reps, same effort = same body.
If nothing is changing in your training, nothing is changing in your results.

4. You’re rushing your reps➡️Fast, sloppy reps = less tension, less control, less results. Slowing down might humble you… but it’s where the growth is.

5. You’re quitting before it works➡️You’ve been consistent for a few weeks… maybe a couple months… and think it’s not working.
Real progress especially muscle and body recomposition takes way longer than people expect.

6. You’re not following a structured program➡️You’re going in with no real direction, just doing what feels right that day. Results come from following a plan not guessing your way through workouts.

If you feel like you’re doing everything… but still not seeing results, it might be time to stop guessing and start following a real plan.

Most people train hard, but miss pieces.
And what you don’t train… doesn’t grow.

Most people turn dumbbell rows into a bicep curl without realizing it. ⬇️ 

If you’re just pulling the weight straight up and down, you’re leaving a lot of lat activation on the table.
Think about rowing the dumbbell back toward your hip, not your shoulder.

Maintain a neutral spine, brace your core, and move with control…no twisting or jerking the weight.
The dumbbell should travel in a slight J-shape, which helps you actually target your lats instead of letting your arms take over.

Remember: heavier isn’t better if the form is off.
Small tweaks in technique = BIG difference in results.

caption:
Most people feel cable crunches in their hip flexors instead of their abs not because the exercise is wrong, but because the movement pattern is off.

If your hips are lifting up and down with each rep, your hip flexors and hamstrings are taking over. That means your core isn’t actually shortening or contracting the way it should.

Here’s the fix:
• Lock your hips in place they stay high and still
• Round through your spine as you crunch
• Think ribs down → belly button toward spine
• Go slow and intentional through each rep

Your abs are a muscle group that needs to shorten to contract.
So the goal isn’t to pull the rope down
It’s to curl your torso and let your core do the work.

Bloating is something almost everyone experiences, and it can be caused by food, stress, or even the way we eat. While quick fixes don’t always work, making small, consistent changes can really help reduce the discomfort. 

Here are 4 simple tips that go a long way:

✨ Practice belly breathing — stress can tighten your core, deep breaths calm the gut.

We often think health = gym + clean eating. And yes, those are important. But the truth is, if stress, rest, joy, and sleep are missing… the body still feels “unwell.”

Your body doesn’t just respond to what you lift or what you eat. It responds to your entire lifestyle. High stress, late nights, and constantly being “on” keep your nervous system in overdrive. That’s why you can work so hard in the gym and still feel drained.

Here are a few ways to bring balance back into your day:
✨ Take 5–10 minutes for stillness, whether that’s meditation, journaling, or simply breathing with no distractions.
✨ Prioritize 7–9 hours of quality sleep. Muscles don’t grow in the gym, they grow when you rest.
✨ Add joy and play into your life. Laughter, connection, and hobbies are powerful antidotes to stress.
✨ Protect your mental energy by creating boundaries with work and technology.

True health isn’t just built through discipline. It’s also built through recovery, presence, and joy. The quiet moments matter just as much as the loud ones. 💫

☑️ Skip the whipped cream and save about 70–80 calories instantly

Uncommon Fitness Tips You Don’t Hear Enough 👇

There’s a lot of noise out there when it comes to fitness advice—
But these are the lesser-known tips that can actually move the needle in your progress:

1. Your nervous system matters.
If you’re always wired, stressed, or underslept, your body won’t respond the way you want it to. Regulating your nervous system through sleep, breathwork, rest, and recovery is a major unlock for performance and results.

2. Tempo creates tension.
It’s not just about the weight you lift—it’s about how you lift it. Slow, controlled reps (especially on the way down) increase time under tension and muscle growth. Don’t rush the rep.

3. Not every session should leave you gasping.
If you’re training at a 10/10 every time, you’re likely overdoing it. Progress needs structure: heavy days, light days, and recovery days. Rest doesn’t mean regression—it means adaptation.

4. Gut health affects your energy and recovery.
A sluggish gut = poor nutrient absorption, low energy, and inflammation. Support your digestion with whole foods, fiber, and stress reduction. What you absorb is more important than what you eat.

5. You don’t have to earn your meals.
Food is fuel. Not a reward. Not a punishment. You’ll make more progress when you stop under-eating and start supporting your body with enough protein, carbs, and calories to actually train and recover.

—

✨ Most people don’t struggle because they’re lazy—they struggle because they’re misinformed.

Save this for the next time you feel stuck, plateaued, or just unsure what’s missing.

But I’ve started to question that programming. To ask: who taught me that I had to be perfect to be loved? Where did I pick up the belief that my value was conditional? And more importantly—am I willing to let that go?

I’ve been doing the slow work of rewiring. Of creating space for grace instead of judgment. Of embracing the awkward, the unfinished, the “good enough.” I’m realizing that freedom doesn’t come from controlling everything—it comes from finally allowing yourself to be as you are.

I’m still in it—still unlearning, still rethinking, still reminding myself daily that softness is not weakness, and that presence is more powerful than perfection. There’s peace in letting go, even if it feels unfamiliar. And maybe that’s the point: the most meaningful growth is rarely comfortable, but it is always honest.
